scope: 26 explicitly queued stranded members; confirmed parent archives were not re-judged.
method: Independent byte inspection, hashes, source control/data-flow review, ZIP local/central headers, in-memory WAR members, bounded bomb decompression; atomscan slow-mode before/after and cleave facts for all 26. cleave strings inspected all source members: no concealed encoded payload recovered. Archive strings unsupported by CLI; bodies were inspected directly. No sample was executed.
path_repair: The Debian extraction was physically rooted at usr/, while the queue names data/usr/. Copied the seven byte-identical members to their exact queue-relative paths before analysis and marking; source hashes match the queued hashes.

members.marker_note: Laudanum PHP command shell: no change
members.behavior: The client IP allowlist precedes SHA-1 password and session-nonce authentication. POST command flows to $command; cd updates session cwd, other commands reach proc_open($command), and both child output streams are escaped into the session terminal. This is an injectable operator-command payload despite its access gates. Legacy curly-brace string indexing and get_magic_quotes_gpc require an older PHP runtime.

members.marker_note: Laudanum WordPress command shell: no change
members.behavior: Includes ipcheck.php, then reads POST command into $command. The execution guard is literal if(true), replacing a commented session-authenticated condition; the login form is disabled with if(false). Commands update cwd or reach proc_open($command), and stdout/stderr return through session output. This template is a reusable command endpoint; its external IP-check include remains an environmental gate. Old PHP syntax limits runtime compatibility.

members.marker_note: WordPress shell plugin: bind reverse-shell sink; detect file locking
members.behavior: At load time, __FILE__ is copied to $this_file, then system() attempts chmod ugo-w and chattr +i on that file. The cmd request value reaches executeCommand(), which tries ReflectionFunction(system)->invoke(), call_user_func_array(), call_user_func(), passthru(), then system(). This is an unauthenticated command endpoint. The alternate intended reverse-shell branch uses undefined $ip/$port request keys and assumes the socket occupies FD 3. Static socket, shell literal and unrelated variable system() calls did not prove that redirected command reaches a sink. The old reverse-shell finding was removed and executed file-locking coverage added. Locking success requires filesystem support and authority; chmod alone does not prevent unlinking.

members.marker_note: Laudanum ASP command shell: no change
members.behavior: Rejects clients whose REMOTE_ADDR differs from the configured IP with a 404. On submission Request.Form("cmd") becomes cmd, WScript.Shell.Exec(cmd) launches the supplied command, and StdOut.ReadAll() returns through Response.Write. The operator may supply cmd.exe /c to enable shell syntax. This is a request-command webshell, without automatic beaconing or outbound networking.

members.marker_note: Laudanum JSP command WAR: no change
members.behavior: Read every ZIP member in memory without deployment: cmd.jsp, WEB-INF/web.xml, META-INF/MANIFEST.MF and directory entries. Both WARs carry identical JSP and web.xml bodies. On GET cmd, Runtime.getRuntime().exec(request.getParameter("cmd")) launches the requested program; its stdout is read line by line and printed to the response. No authentication guard exists. XML schema URLs are declarations, not network callbacks. The member table and deflate content prove an actual deployable request-command payload rather than a filename-only indicator.

members.marker_note: Overlapping ZIP64 decompression bomb: no change
members.behavior: Parsed 190023 members declaring 4507981427706459 unpacked bytes (about 4.5 PB) in 45876952 input bytes. Local and central ZIP64 records identify overlapping compressed streams with a shared end offset 34144784. For example, member 0 data begins at 51, and the next local header begins at 56, inside that stream. Bounded raw-deflate decoding of selected streams recovered real content; the last member yields repeated byte 0x61. This is shared-stream amplification, not recursive ZIP nesting or merely a large legitimate archive. Full expansion was deliberately avoided.

members.marker_note: Root UID tiny shell source: no change
members.behavior: main() requests real, effective and saved UID zero using setresuid(0,0,0), then launches /bin/sh through system(). There is no credential gate, privilege-drop path, argument validation or networking. This is a minimal root-shell backdoor stub. It needs inherited root authority, setuid installation or suitable capabilities: these calls cannot give an ordinary unprivileged process root by themselves. The source was not compiled or executed.

members.marker_note: Pentestmonkey WordPress reverse shell: no change
members.behavior: Optionally forks and calls setsid(), changes cwd to /, clears umask, connects an outbound fsockopen socket, and proc_open launches uname -a; w; id; /bin/sh -i with three pipes. Nonblocking stream_select drives explicit copies from socket reads into child stdin, and child stdout/stderr into the same socket. This is a real bidirectional reverse-shell stream bridge, not independent socket and process APIs. No encoding or encrypted C2 exists. POST ip/port select the destination, with fallback 10.2.2.1:8888.

members.marker_note: PHP extracted-request dispatch shell: no change
members.behavior: Executable body is @extract($_REQUEST); @die($ctime($atime));. Default extract imports request keys as local variables, allowing the caller to select both the function name (ctime=system, for example) and its argument (atime). The selected function runs before die consumes its result, and functions such as system directly emit command output. The timestamp-like variable names and suppressed errors conceal an unrestricted callback surface; no decoding is needed. There is no credential or IP guard.

regression_expectation_correction: The existing php-indirect-request-command-shell.php fixture executes a request command but only sends its redirected-shell string with fwrite(sock, shell). It does not execute that string. Retained the command-webshell requirement, forbade the reverse-shell finding, and adjusted the old two-hostile score floor accordingly.
